title: Printers & scanners
blurb: Offline, stuck jobs, wrong printer, scanning.

remedies.title: Printer says "Offline"
remedies.why: The computer can't reach the printer: it's asleep, on another Wi-Fi, got a new network address, or a job is stuck.

steps.text: Wake the printer and check its screen for errors (paper, toner, jam). Turn it off and on.
Make sure the printer and computer are on the same Wi-Fi network (printers often fall back to a setup network).
Clear stuck jobs and restart the print service.
Open Printers & scanners › the printer › Open print queue; if it shows "Use printer offline" ticked, untick it.
Open Printers & Scanners, select the printer › Printer Queue › Resume.
Remove the printer and add it again; the system will find its new address.

remedies.escalate: For an office printer, tell IT its name/number and whether others can print to it.

remedies.title: Print jobs are stuck in the queue
remedies.why: A damaged job blocks everything behind it.

steps.text: Clear the whole queue and restart the print spooler (one click).
Open the printer's queue, delete the jobs, and press Resume.
Turn the printer off and on, then print again.

remedies.title: Add a printer
remedies.why: Most printers on the same network are found automatically; older ones need their driver.

steps.text: Connect the printer to the same Wi-Fi as the computer (using its own screen or app).
Settings › Bluetooth & devices › Printers & scanners › Add device.
Printers & Scanners › Add Printer, Scanner or Fax… and pick it from the list.
If it isn't listed, add it by its IP address (print a network configuration page from the printer to find it).
At work, add shared printers the way IT tells you (a print server address or a company portal).

remedies.title: Prints go to the wrong printer
remedies.why: Windows can switch the default to the last printer used; or another printer was set as the default.

steps.text: Turn off "Let Windows manage my default printer", then choose the printer › Set as default.
Printers & Scanners › Default printer.
Check the printer chosen in each app's print dialog; apps remember the last one.

remedies.title: Printer prints blank, faded or streaky pages
remedies.why: Empty or dried ink/toner, clogged print heads, or the wrong paper setting.

steps.text: Check ink or toner levels on the printer's screen or app; replace empties.
Run the printer's own cleaning or alignment tool (from its menu or app); repeat once if needed.
Gently shake a laser toner cartridge side to side.
Print a test page from the printer itself; if that's bad too, the printer needs service.

remedies.title: Paper jam (even when there's no paper stuck)
remedies.why: A torn scrap stays inside, or paper is loaded crooked or too full.

steps.text: Turn the printer off before reaching inside. Open every door and tray, pull paper out slowly in the direction it travels.
Look with a torch for small torn pieces near the rollers.
Reload fewer sheets, squared up, with the guides snug, and use the paper type the tray is set to.

remedies.title: Scanner not found or scanning doesn't start
remedies.why: The scanner part needs its own driver or app, or it's on a different network.

steps.text: Scan with the Windows Scan app or the printer maker's app (HP Smart, Epson ScanSmart, Canon PRINT…).
Use Printers & Scanners › the printer › Scan, or Image Capture / Preview › File › Import from Scanner.
Remove and re-add the printer so the scanner driver installs too.
Scan to email or a USB stick from the printer's screen as a workaround.

remedies.title: Printout is the wrong size, cut off or tiny
remedies.why: The paper size in the document, the print dialog and the printer tray don't match (often A4 vs Letter).

steps.text: In the print dialog set the paper size to what's in the tray, and Scale to Fit.
Set the tray's paper size on the printer's own screen to match.
Check the document's own page size (Word: Layout › Size).

remedies.title: Printer prints gibberish or a driver error
remedies.why: The wrong or a damaged printer driver is installed.

steps.text: Clear the print queue.
Remove the printer: Printers & scanners › the printer › Remove.
Remove its driver too: Print Management › All Drivers › delete the printer's driver (if available), or Print server properties › Drivers.
Add the printer again, using the driver from the maker's website for your exact model.
